subject: Re: Redwood model fit + benchmarks for Pangea Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.coale@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@pangeahealth.com>, Alex Kim <alex.kim@pangeahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood model fit + benchmarks follow-up (post-call recap)

Hi Sanjay / Alex — great to meet today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery call: 

Summary of needs
- Primary use case: clinical triage assistant to summarize intake forms and surface likely care pathways.
- SLA targets: sub-200ms p50 for single-turn queries; tolerate higher tails for complex long-context jobs but want p95 <= 800ms when possible.
- Throughput: anticipated steady-state ~150 qps, bursts to ~400 qps during peak sign-up windows.
- Data constraints: PHI, on-prem/private deployment desirable but open to Dedicated depending on contract/SLA.

Model fit recommendation (initial)
- Recommendation A (latency-optimized): rw-open-1.3b-q4f (low latency, high TPS, best for extraction & short summarization).
- Recommendation B (quality/longer-context): rw-opt-13b-8bit (better instruction following on longer prompts, higher accuracy on clinical language).

Benchmarks & artifacts shared
- Redwood-verified performance profiles (TPS, latency percentiles) attached + hosted: https://app.redwood.ai/benchmarks/pangeahealth-2026-v1
- Example prompt set we used for evaluation: prompt_set_healthcare.txt (attached).
- CSV of raw benchmark runs: redwood_bench_v1.csv (attached).

Open questions / asks
1) Would you be able to share a representative sample (anonymized) of 500–1,000 intake prompts so we can run a quick in-house eval against your SLOs?
2) Which compliance mode do you prefer for pilot: Dedicated (customer-isolated) or Private (VPC/on-prem) — we can scope cost/lead times once you confirm.
3) Any hard constraints on p95 latency for long-context summarization?

Proposed next steps
- I’ll loop in Rishi to share the Redwood-verified perf profile summary and any prompt-level quality notes.
- If sample prompts are OK, we’ll run a focused eval and share a short exec summary + recommended model & config.
- Schedule a 30-min technical session next week to review results and pilot options.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications before we send the sample prompts: 

- When you say p95 <= 800ms for the latency-optimized model, is that measured at 150 qps or at the higher burst rate? We care about steady-state more than bursts.
- Do you have any examples in the prompt set of multi-turn adjudication (context + appended clinician notes)? If not, I’ll flag that as an ask.

We can provide anonymized intake prompts; I’ll check with security but expect OK for 500 records.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 10:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood model fit + benchmarks follow-up (post-call recap)

Hi Sanjay / Alex — following up with the technical summary and answers to your latency questions. Summary below is from Redwood-verified runs using your target prompt patterns (short: triage Q&A, medium: 2–3 turn context, long: intake + clinician note appended). Raw CSV attached.

Short summary (recommended configs)
- rw-open-1.3b-q4f (latency-optimized)
  - Measured TPS at 150 concurrent qps: sustained ~165–175 qps (we reserve headroom).
  - Latency percentiles (single-turn, 512 token cap): p50 ~45 ms, p95 ~220 ms, p99 ~420 ms.
  - Notes: Excellent cost/TPS; quality strong on extraction and short summarization; degrades slightly on long multi-turn clinical reasoning.

- rw-opt-13b-8bit (quality-optimized)
  - Measured TPS at 150 concurrent qps: sustained ~18–22 qps on a single Dedicated shard; can autoscale across shards for throughput.
  - Latency percentiles (single-turn, 1024 token cap): p50 ~380 ms, p95 ~780 ms, p99 ~1.6 s.
  - Notes: Best-in-class instruction-following and long-context accuracy vs 1.3b but higher cost and tail latency.

Quality/regression notes
- We ran the supplied prompt set (attached) plus an internal clinical prompt bank. There were a couple of prompt patterns where the 1.3b model missed nested entity extraction (~4% failure rate) while the 13b reduced failures to ~1.2%.
- We recommend running a focused eval on your 500 anonymized examples to measure your task-level metrics (precision/recall) so we can size the right model and any prompting/ensemble strategies.

Pilot config suggestions
- Phase 1 (pilot): Start with rw-open-1.3b-q4f on Redwood Dedicated with autoscale to handle peak bursts; use prefix caching for repeated templates. Run the focused eval on your 500 prompts and produce a quality/latency tradeoff report.
- Phase 2 (expanded): For high-risk/complex cases, route to rw-opt-13b-8bit (can be a fallback route or used for post-hoc verification).

Artifacts and links
- Full perf profile: https://app.redwood.ai/benchmarks/pangeahealth-2026-v1 (includes histograms and raw RK runs).
- Prompt set for our eval: prompt_set_healthcare.txt (attached).
- Raw benchmark CSV: redwood_bench_v1.csv (attached).

Next steps
- If you confirm we can get 500 anonymized prompts, we’ll run the focused eval and return a 1–2 page exec summary within 3 business days.
- If you prefer, we can provision a short-term Dedicated trial (7 days) so you can run live traffic tests; Marissa can share pricing options.

Happy to jump on a short tech sync next week to walk through the perf dashboards.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
